long_biography.plain_text:
Ukraine’s government is centred on the Cabinet of Ministers, the highest body in the country’s executive system. It implements national policy and coordinates ministries and other executive agencies. The database name therefore identifies a continuing public institution, not an officeholder or a private asset owner.

Krym entered Ukrainian service after the Soviet Union dissolved and became BG01 with the Ukrainian Sea Guard. Built as a Project 1360 special-service ship, it supported protection and transport duties involving senior state officials. The vessel left Crimea for Odesa in 2014 and was later assigned to the Sea Guard training system for cadet practice. Its history reflects state stewardship through a border-security agency rather than personal ownership of a private asset.

uncertainties.detail: Ukraine Government is a broad database label rather than the formal name of a single asset-holding legal entity. The Constitution identifies the Cabinet of Ministers as the government and highest executive body, while Krym has been administered through the State Border Guard Service's Sea Guard. The dossier therefore retains the immutable umbrella label and describes agency stewardship without renaming the owner or substituting an officeholder.

The authoritative relationship record and some commercial yacht directories report Krym as 40 metres and 290 GT. SuperYacht Times and Project 1360 histories report 45.3 metres and the same 290 GT, matching BG01's 8.94-metre beam and 1978 Almaz build. The shared name, builder, tonnage, special-service history and 1992 Ukraine transfer resolve the vessel identity, but no owner-field correction is proposed or applied.

Some commercial directory pages summarize Krym as a 1980 build. Ukrainian specialist reporting dates its keel to 1977, launch to 16 August 1978 and commissioning to 31 August 1978; SuperYacht Times also uses 1978. The biographies avoid the disputed summary year.

A 2019 Sea Guard announcement documented the decision to convert Krym for training, and an official Border Guard photograph described BG01 as a training vessel in Odesa in March 2021. Detailed operational status after the full-scale invasion is not publicly disclosed. The biography says the vessel was assigned to training, not that it is currently operational or available.

Public sources consistently establish state service, but use several formulations: Government of Ukraine, presidential or government yacht, State Border Guard Service and Ukrainian Sea Guard. These describe sovereign ownership and agency administration rather than competing private beneficial owners. No current or former president is treated as the owner.

Honorific, middle name, gender, birth and death fields are inapplicable to this public institution. Institution dossiers may not propose personal social links, so official government and Border Guard pages remain research sources rather than proposed profiles.

No dedicated Forbes institution-owner profile was found. All four wealth classifications are Unknown because public authority, state property and budget stewardship are not private wealth mechanisms; this is a non-applicability decision rather than an evidence gap.

Government-owned is the sole proposed tag because the owner record is the sovereign public body itself and Krym is a state-service asset. Shipping, yachting, military, politician or officeholder tags would misstate the institutional relationship or fall outside the approved semantic contracts.
